key_insight: LSPO trains a model to learn from the quality of state transitions—not just final answers—by combining a lifted continuous state, energy-based ranking, and self-correction internalization.
engineering_relevance: It offers a single-pass alternative to test-time reflection that can preserve accuracy while reducing latency and token usage, which is attractive for deploying reasoning systems efficiently.
method: Augment each answer with a learned continuous coordinate to form a lifted state.
Use an energy function and shaped reward to favor low-cost transitions toward better reasoning states.
Internalize selected low-energy answers into the direct generator via an auxiliary loss.
evidence_signal: On Qwen3.5-27B, LSPO reached 71.8% aggregate accuracy across math, science, code, and logic benchmarks, essentially matching test-time reflection at 71.9% while using 28% less latency and 25.8% fewer tokens.
watch_item: The approach adds learned latent-state machinery and cost shaping, so performance may depend on careful tuning of transition, edit, and internalization weights.
paper_title: Lifted State Policy Optimization: Internalizing Self-Correction through Transition Geometry
